name: Manaen
overview: Manaen was a male prophet and teacher in the early Christian church at Antioch, noted for his role in the community as described in Acts 13:1. He is uniquely identified as having been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, indicating a background connected to the Herodian royal family. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or surname.
namesAndTitles: The name Manaen means 'comforter' and is recorded as a proper name in Acts 13:1. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it reflects a meaningful personal designation within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Manaen beyond what is noted about his upbringing with Herod the tetrarch. No other familial connections are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Manaen's significance in the New Testament lies in his role as a prophet and teacher in the Antioch church, a key center for the early Christian mission. His upbringing alongside Herod the tetrarch suggests he had a unique social background, which may have influenced his ministry. His presence among the leaders in Acts 13:1 highlights the diverse composition of the early church's ministry team.
